Hi Taylor — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary answers below and I attached a revised SIG sheet and a simple data-flow diagram as requested. See inline for links to evidence.

1) Retention: Default hosted API retention for request/response logs ("prompt logs") is 30 days for our self-serve and standard hosted tiers. For enterprise/Dedicated customers we support configurable retention windows up to 13 months and can implement contractually required retention windows (including custom deletion schedules).

2) Training on customer content: Redwood does NOT use customer content (prompts, responses, embeddings, or files) to train or improve model weights by default. We treat training on customer data as an explicit, opt-in process only available under a separate written agreement with controls (data scope, blinding/aggregation, and deletion guarantees).

3) Deletion/erasure: For hosted customers, deletion requests are handled via our support portal and an automated backend job; standard SLA is 30 days to fully remove accessible copies from live serving storage and caches, and 90 days to complete background archival purges for long-term backups (if any backups exist for that tenant). For enterprise contracts we can shorten SLAs and provide deletion certificates.

Evidence and links:
- Updated SIG answers (attached): redwood_sig_answers_v2.xlsx
- Data flow & storage diagram (attached): redwood_data_flow_diagram.png
- SOC 2 report & data handling summary: https://redwood-inference.share/SOC2-report-2025
- Public docs section on prompt logs & retention: https://redwood-inference.docs/data-handling#prompt-logs

I copied Vivek (Security) and Laura (Account lead) to ensure we can commit to whatever contractual language you need. If you want, we can schedule a short call to walk compliance through the diagram.

Hi Taylor — Vivek from Security here. Quick technical confirmations and contractual options below. Copying Laura for SOW language and Marcus for Dedicated/region specifics.

Encryption & backups:
- All prompt logs and customer content are encrypted at rest using AES-256. Customer keys are managed by Redwood KMS by default. For enterprise customers we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via supported KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- Backups/snapshots: For hosted tiers backups are encrypted and reside in the same cloud region(s) as the tenant by default; we do not replicate hosted customer backups to other global regions without customer agreement. For Dedicated/private deployments the customer controls the backup location.

Opt-in training pathway:
- Training on customer data is an add-on service that requires a written agreement and a minimum 6-month term. Customers receive: (a) scoped data ingestion plan, (b) ability to exempt specific datasets or labels, (c) a deletion certificate for contributed slices post-project, and (d) an audit report showing data handling steps.

Shorter deletion SLA / SOW language:
- We can commit to a 7-day deletion SLA for specific regulated data classes under enterprise addendum and with appropriate statement of work language. Laura will produce suggested SOW wording for inclusion (example below).

Data residency for logs:
- Default: US-only regions for US tenants. We will include a one-line SOW clause: "Log storage and backups for this SOW will be restricted to US regions unless explicit cross-region replication is requested and approved." Laura — attaching suggested SOW text in a follow-up.

If you want an RACI or a short runbook for the deletion flow, we can share that as well.
